clean_source_blocks.text: Kramnik has said he will appeal the decision The World Chess Federation (Fide) has banned former world champion Kramnik for at least a year over verbal attacks he made on other players, including the late Daniel Naroditsky. The body said it had found Kramnik "responsible for multiple violations" of its ethics and disciplinary code after the Russian accused other players of cheating. US grandmaster Naroditsky died last October at the age of 29. Before his death, he had denied any wrongdoing and indicated the controversy had taken its toll on him in his final Twitch broadcast. Kramnik wrote on X that he will appeal his suspension. Another 12 months of the ban have been suspended for a probationary period of three years, Fide said. It means the active suspension is one year provided no further breaches occur during probation.
The former Russian world chess champion had accused other players, including the late Daniel Naroditsky, of cheating.

Former world champion Vladimir Kramnik has been suspended by the international governing body for chess for at least a year after he levelled unproven allegations of cheating against fellow players, including Daniel Naroditsky. Kramnik accused Naroditsky, who died last year at age 29, of cheating last year and continued to share suspicions on social media. Naroditsky, a prodigious chess player and American grandmaster who helped usher in the game's online boom with educational YouTube videos and livestreams, denied the allegations. Kramnik said he plans to appeal the suspension. "I am absolutely confident that this unlawful verdict will ultimately be overturned, and I intend to pursue all necessary instances to the very end in order to restore justice and, in particular, my reputation," Kramnik said.

Naroditsky was a popular player, teacher and commentator. He was a leading figure in online chess with hundreds of thousands of followers - who knew him as Danya - across Twitch and YouTube. A toxicology report released in 2026 said he had had multiple drugs in his system at the time and was killed by an abnormal heartbeat caused by an accidental overdose. Some prominent figures in the chess community - including world number two Hikaru Nakamura, former world champion Magnus Carlsen and Indian grandmaster Nihal Sarin - have previously condemned Kramnik's conduct. Naroditsky had hundreds of thousands of followers across YouTube and Twitch. Fide said its findings were not intended to determine the validity of Kramnik's remarks, but were concerned with the manner in which the allegations were communicated publicly.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Kramnik has said he will appeal the decision

The World Chess Federation (Fide) has banned former world champion Kramnik for at least a year over verbal attacks he made on other players, including the late Daniel Naroditsky.

The body said it had found Kramnik "responsible for multiple violations" of its ethics and disciplinary code after the Russian accused other players of cheating.

US grandmaster Naroditsky died last October at the age of 29. Before his death, he had denied any wrongdoing and indicated the controversy had taken its toll on him in his final Twitch broadcast.

Kramnik wrote on X that he will appeal his suspension.

Another 12 months of the ban have been suspended for a probationary period of three years, Fide said. It means the active suspension is one year provided no further breaches occur during probation.

Naroditsky was a popular player, teacher and commentator. He was a leading figure in online chess with hundreds of thousands of followers - who knew him as Danya - across Twitch and YouTube.

A toxicology report released in 2026 said he had had multiple drugs in his system at the time and was killed by an abnormal heartbeat caused by an accidental overdose.

Some prominent figures in the chess community - including world number two Hikaru Nakamura, former world champion Magnus Carlsen and Indian grandmaster Nihal Sarin - have previously condemned Kramnik's conduct.

Naroditsky had hundreds of thousands of followers across YouTube and Twitch.

Fide said its findings were not intended to determine the validity of Kramnik's remarks, but were concerned with the manner in which the allegations were communicated publicly.

The chess body said combating cheating remained one of its highest priorities, but it stressed that such allegations must be handled through its established procedures.

Kramnik was the world champion from 2000-07 and is a self-declared "advocate for fair play in chess".

Naroditsky earned the title of grandmaster - the international chess federation's highest-ranked chess competitor - while he was still a teenager, after winning the 2013 US Junior Championship.

Chess federation looking into Vladimir Kramnik's attacks on grandmaster Daniel Naroditsky

---

[Lähde: AOL]
Former world champion Vladimir Kramnik has been suspended by the international governing body for chess for at least a year after he levelled unproven allegations of cheating against fellow players, including Daniel Naroditsky.

Kramnik accused Naroditsky, who died last year at age 29, of cheating last year and continued to share suspicions on social media. Naroditsky, a prodigious chess player and American grandmaster who helped usher in the game's online boom with educational YouTube videos and livestreams, denied the allegations.

Kramnik said he plans to appeal the suspension.

"I am absolutely confident that this unlawful verdict will ultimately be overturned, and I intend to pursue all necessary instances to the very end in order to restore justice and, in particular, my reputation," Kramnik said.

The International Chess Federation (FIDE) said Kramnik publicly alleged cheating without "adequate evidentiary support," violating its rules against cyberbullying.

The federation said combating cheating was one of its priorities, but that allegations must be addressed through its procedures and supported by appropriate evidence.

"He exposed identifiable players to unjustified reputational harm and undermined the safeguards established by the disciplinary framework," federation representatives said in their decision.

Naroditsky was found dead at his North Carolina home in October. He was killed by an abnormal heartbeat caused by an accidental overdose, according to a toxicology report.

Naroditsky had said before his death that Kramnik's allegations had taken a toll on him.

"Ever since the Kramnik stuff, I feel like if I start doing well, people assume the worst of intentions. The issue is just the lingering effect of it," Naroditsky said in his last livestream before his death.

Kramnik called Naroditsky's death a tragedy. He said there had been a cynical campaign to link him to Naroditsky's death without any factual basis.

payload.title: Fide määräsi Vladimir Kramnikille vähintään vuoden kilpailukiellon huijaussyytöksistä
payload.summary: Kansainvälinen shakkiliitto Fide on asettanut entisen maailmanmestarin Vladimir Kramnikin vähintään vuoden kilpailukieltoon muiden pelaajien julkisesta syyttämisestä huijaamisesta.
payload.content:
Kansainvälinen shakkiliitto Fide on määrännyt entiselle shakin maailmanmestarille Vladimir Kramnikille vähintään vuoden kilpailukiellon sen jälkeen, kun hän oli esittänyt julkisia huijaussyytöksiä muita pelaajia vastaan. Syytösten kohteisiin kuului yhdysvaltalainen suurmestari Daniel Naroditsky, joka kuoli viime vuonna 29-vuotiaana.

## Fide: kyse oli väitteiden esittämistavasta

Fiden mukaan Kramnik oli vastuussa useista liiton eettisten ja kurinpitosääntöjen rikkomuksista. Liitto korosti, ettei sen ratkaisu ollut kannanotto siihen, pitivätkö Kramnikin väitteet paikkansa, vaan siihen, millä tavalla syytöksiä esitettiin julkisesti.

Kramnik oli syyttänyt Naroditskya ja muita pelaajia huijaamisesta ja jatkanut epäilyjensä jakamista sosiaalisessa mediassa. Naroditsky kiisti ennen kuolemaansa tehneensä mitään väärää. Hänen kerrottiin myös viitanneen viimeisessä Twitch-lähetyksessään siihen, että kohu oli kuormittanut häntä.

Fiden määräämä aktiivinen kilpailukielto kestää vuoden, jos uusia rikkomuksia ei tapahdu koeaikana. Lisäksi toinen 12 kuukauden kielto on ehdollinen kolmen vuoden koeajalla, joten Kramnikin pidempi seuraamus riippuu siitä, rikkooko hän sääntöjä koeajan aikana.

## Kramnik aikoo valittaa päätöksestä

Kramnik on ilmoittanut aikovansa valittaa päätöksestä. Hän kirjoitti X:ssä olevansa varma, että hänen mukaansa lainvastainen ratkaisu lopulta kumotaan, ja sanoi vievänsä asian tarvittaessa loppuun asti oikeudenmukaisuuden ja maineensa palauttamiseksi.

Naroditsky oli tunnettu pelaaja, opettaja ja kommentaattori. Hän oli näkyvä hahmo verkossa pelattavan shakin nousussa, ja hänellä oli satojatuhansia seuraajia YouTubessa ja Twitchissä, joissa monet tunsivat hänet nimellä Danya.

Vuonna 2026 julkaistun toksikologisen raportin mukaan Naroditskyn elimistössä oli kuoleman hetkellä useita aineita, ja hänen kuolemansa johtui epänormaalista sydämenrytmistä, jonka aiheutti tapaturmainen yliannostus.

## Shakkiyhteisö oli arvostellut Kramnikia

Useat tunnetut shakkivaikuttajat olivat jo aiemmin arvostelleet Kramnikin toimintaa. Lähteissä mainittuihin arvostelijoihin kuuluivat maailmanlistan kakkonen Hikaru Nakamura, entinen maailmanmestari Magnus Carlsen ja intialainen suurmestari Nihal Sarin.
